column1: # token_hash pairs against an rq checkout (run from ~/code/lib/rust/rq).
# DRAFTED BY CLAUDE, NOT YET REVIEWED BY THE OWNER. Verified by reading both
# bodies. See tests/eval/rust/trekr/pairs.tsv and the README for the tier's
# contract and the same-id convention.
# HISTORY: this set originally labeled rq's epoch-seconds family (now_secs /
# unix_now / now_unix twice) — two duplicates and the qualification twin. On
# 2026-08-27 rq consolidated all four into core/clock.rs (7df14e2, "One
# clock, not four"), which is the outcome dupes exists to cause: the labels
# were retired WITH the duplication. The qualification-twin contract case
# (path-qualified vs imported names are different tokens, correct-by-design)
# is no longer instantiable here; rwr's renamed-local rows still cover the
# normalization boundary.
# The one exact group in today's checkout is tests::empty_and_unparseable_
# yield_no_symbols, copied across FOUR language plugins' inline test mods.
# It is deliberately NOT labeled: all four units share one id under DEC-012's
# owner rule, and the same-id convention is only sound for exactly two.
# (Those inline #[cfg(test)] mods also classify as `app` — DEC-022's
# standing example — so the test population banner cannot separate them.)
# Per-plugin extract calls its own module's grammar and walker: one differing
# token (tree_sitter_go vs tree_sitter_rust) that is the entire behaviour.
lang::rust::Rust::extract
# Byte-identical `LANGUAGE` bodies that each resolve to their OWN module's
# constant — Rust's version of rails' constant-scope pair, and DEC-020 calls
# it distinct: the trait method IS the per-plugin datum. The tier currently
# groups them below --min-lines 4 (3 lines), so the default floor is what
# hides the false positive.
lang::go::Go::language
